title: Sample the actual first decoded video frame, not t=0.25 seconds
root_cause: The existing authenticated Netlify video extractor labelled the first sampled frame at min(0.25,max(0.05,duration*0.05)) as 'start'. For 8 second reels this samples at 0.25s, not t=0. As a result, a producer's literal master first-frame claim was never checked at frame zero. This does not explain separately failed midpoint face scores.
impact: False interpretation of t=0.25 face-score rejections as direct evidence about literal frame zero and non-reproducible identity drift analysis.
fix: Extract the first decoded video frame from timestamp 0 through existing ffmpeg and keep midpoint/end sampling unchanged. No video modification, replay, provider publishing, vision threshold or identity whitelist changes.
prevention_rule: Where evidence is named a first or initial video frame, require sample offset zero with an executable regression. Preserve canonical 0.94 start/middle/end verification and temporal/provider proofs.
release_gates: Protected merge and Netlify production source artifact/readback
Only rerun existing canonical verified media proof on a fresh eligible candidate
Real Instagram external post ID and independent provider readback for LIVE_PROVEN
outcome: CANDIDATE only; no Instagram provider post and no revenue snapshot repair
